title: Review: Fuerza Gym
paragraphs: Fuerza Gym, Mexico City – 3 stars out of 5
I joined Fuerza Gym two months ago. I'm twenty-two, and I wanted to get stronger before my new job. The membership costs 650 pesos a month, which is cheaper than the gym near my office.

The equipment is good. There are enough machines, and I never wait more than five minutes. The changing rooms are clean, and the showers are hot. The trainers are friendly and always ready to help beginners, so I didn't feel embarrassed on my first day.

However, the gym isn't perfect. It gets very crowded after six in the evening, and there isn't enough air conditioning. Last week the lockers weren't working, so I left my bag at the desk. Also, the app for booking classes is too slow.
Overall, it's a good gym for the price. My advice: go early in the morning, bring your own towel and ask a trainer for a free plan. I give it three stars out of five.

title: A Day near Cotopaxi
paragraphs: Friday, 5:00 a.m. We left Quito in a small van with our guide, Luis. There were six of us. It was cold and dark, and nobody spoke much.

Friday, 10:30 a.m. We walked for three hours, and the view was amazing. A cloud covered the top of the volcano, but then the sun came out. My friend Andrés felt dizzy because we were very high, so we stopped and drank some water.
Friday, 2:00 p.m. We ate lunch next to a lake. The guide gave us a sandwich and an apple. Everything was in the price of 45 dollars, but I paid ten dollars more for a jacket because I forgot mine.

Friday, 9:00 p.m. I'm at home now, and my legs hurt. It was the most beautiful day of my year. I took a hundred photos, but the best memory isn't in a photo: it's the silence on the mountain. Next month we're going to climb a smaller volcano.

title: A Room in Madrid
paragraphs: Dear Mrs Ortega,
My name is Hugo Ramírez, and I'm a student from Chile. I saw your advert for a room in Madrid on a website yesterday. I'm very interested because I'm starting a one-year course in September.

I have a few questions. First, how much is the rent? The advert says 420 euros, but I'd like to know if the bills are included. Second, is the room big enough for a desk? I need a quiet place to study. Third, how far is it from the metro?
I'm a tidy person, and I don't smoke. I like cooking, but I always clean the kitchen after dinner. I don't have any pets.
I'm arriving in Madrid on 28 August, so I can visit the flat on the thirtieth. Could we meet in the morning? I can also send you a reference from my last landlord.
Thank you for your time. I hope to hear from you soon.
Best wishes,
Hugo Ramírez

title: Local Team Wins Robotics Competition
paragraphs: A team of four students from a school in Guadalajara won first prize at the National Robotics Competition last Saturday. The competition took place in Mexico City, and more than sixty teams came to take part.

The students, aged sixteen and seventeen, built a robot that collects rubbish from the floor. It was designed in just three months. 'We worked every afternoon after school,' said team captain Renata Cruz. 'Sometimes we stayed until ten at night.'

At first, the robot didn't work well. In the first round, it stopped after two minutes because a wire came loose. The team fixed it in twenty minutes, and in the final round the robot collected twelve objects in only three minutes.

The winners received a trophy and 20,000 pesos. They are using the money to buy new parts for next year's competition. Their teacher, Mr Salinas, said, 'I'm very proud of them. They worked really hard.'

title: Julián, the Street Drummer
paragraphs: Julián Pérez, thirty, plays the drums in the old town of Cartagena, Colombia. Tourists stop, film him and clap. We asked him about his life.
Interviewer: What did you use to do before music?
Julián: I used to work in a bank. I sat at a desk for nine hours a day, and I was always tired. I didn't hate it, but I wasn't happy.
Interviewer: When did you start playing the drums?
Julián: When I was twelve, I used to play on plastic buckets in my grandmother's yard. She never said anything, which was lucky!
Interviewer: Is it a good job?
Julián: Some days are great. On a Saturday, I can earn 150,000 pesos. But on rainy days, I earn nothing, so I always keep some money for those days.
Interviewer: What's your advice for young musicians?
Julián: Practise every day, and don't be afraid of people. The first time I played in the street, my hands were shaking, but now I love it.

title: A Ten-Minute Study Plan
paragraphs: Many students study for hours and learn very little. Here is a simple plan for your next exam. It takes only ten minutes to prepare.
Step 1: Choose one subject. Don't try to study Maths, History and English in the same afternoon. Write the topic on a piece of paper.
Step 2: Put your phone in another room. If you can't do that, turn it to silent and put it face down. Notifications break your concentration.
Step 3: Study for twenty-five minutes. Then take a five-minute break. Stand up, drink some water or look out of the window. After four sessions, take a longer break of twenty minutes.
Step 4: At the end, close your book and write three things that you remember. This is much more useful than reading the same page again and again.
Tip: Don't study late at night. You need at least eight hours of sleep. Tomorrow your brain will work better.

title: The Last Bus in Cusco
paragraphs: It was nine o'clock at night, and Lucía was waiting for the last bus in Cusco. It was raining, and the street was empty. She was wearing a thin jacket, and she was holding a box of books for her aunt.
While she was checking her phone, a small dog came out from behind a wall. It was wet, and it was shaking. Lucía gave it half of her sandwich. The dog ate it in two seconds.
When the bus arrived, the driver said, 'No animals.' Lucía didn't know what to do. She couldn't leave the dog alone in the rain, so she paid ten soles for a taxi instead.
At her aunt's house, everybody was watching a football match. When they saw the dog, they all stood up. Her aunt said, 'You can keep it until we find the owner.'

The next day, they saw a note on a lamp post: 'Lost dog – Pancho – 50 soles reward'. The owner, an old man, was crying when he saw Pancho. He gave Lucía the money, but she didn't take it. 'I just want to visit him sometimes,' she said. 'Of course,' he answered.

title: Speak Up! Language Exchange Club
paragraphs: Do you want to practise English? Join Speak Up! in Córdoba, Argentina.

Every Thursday from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. we meet at Café Alameda, on San Martín Street. For half of the evening we speak English, and for the other half we speak Spanish. English speakers from different countries come to learn Spanish, so you can practise with real people.
Who can join? Anybody over sixteen. You don't need a perfect level: beginners are very welcome. Our members are students, workers and travellers.
Cost: The first evening is free. After that, the membership is 3,000 pesos a month, and you get a coffee at half price.
What do we do? We play word games, talk about films and music, and sometimes we go for a walk in the park. Once a month we have a quiz night with small prizes.
How to join: Send a message to our page or just come on Thursday! Don't be shy. Everybody makes mistakes, and that's how we learn.

title: A Year Without Meat
focus: Quantifiers: much, many, a few, a little
paragraphs: One year ago I decided to stop eating meat. I live in São Paulo, a city with a lot of excellent steak restaurants, so my friends thought I was crazy.

At the beginning, it was hard. I didn't know many recipes, and I ate too much pasta. I also didn't have much energy because I wasn't eating enough protein. A doctor helped me, and now I eat lots of beans, eggs, nuts and vegetables.

Surprisingly, it isn't more expensive. A kilo of beans costs about 8 reais, and a kilo of beef costs 45 reais. I spend a little less money on food every month, and I have a few new favourite dishes, like lentil soup.
Of course, there are some problems. When I visit my grandmother, she always prepares meat, and she doesn't understand me. Last Sunday she cooked a special rice with vegetables for me. I almost cried!
Is it for everybody? No, and I don't tell people what to eat. But if you are curious, try one meatless day a week. You might like it.

title: Podcast Review: Two Friends, One Microphone
paragraphs: 4 stars out of 5

I started listening to this podcast three months ago, and now I never miss an episode. Two friends, Chloe from London and Sam from Sydney, talk about everyday topics: food, football, holidays and bad days at work. Each episode is only twelve minutes long, so it's perfect for the bus.

The best thing is the speed. They speak clearly, but not too slowly, so you hear natural English. At the end of each episode, they repeat five useful expressions. I write them in a notebook and try to use them the next day.

There are also some problems. Sometimes they make jokes that I don't understand, and their accents are very different. At first, I wanted to stop listening, but then I found a transcript on their website. It's free, and it helps a lot.
I recommend this podcast for people at A2 or B1 level. It isn't as difficult as the news, and it's more fun than a textbook. Listen to three episodes before you decide.
